about: The epistola of the formulary “Nativity of the Lord — Mass during the Day” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: In many portions and in many ways God spoke of old to the fathers in the prophets; at last, in these days, He has spoken to us in the Son, whom He established as heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages; who, being the splendor of His glory and the form of His substance, and bearing all things by His word of power, making the cleansing of sins, sits on high at the right hand of the Majesty, having been made as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is more distinguished than theirs. For to which of the angels did He ever say: You are my Son, today I have begotten You? And once more: I will be a father to Him, and He will be a son to me? And when He again brings the firstborn into the world, He says: And let all God’s angels adore Him. And concerning the angels He indeed says: Who makes His angels into spirits, and His ministers into a flame of fire. Yet to the Son: O God, Your throne is for ever and ever; the rod of Your kingdom is a rod of equity. You have loved justice and hated iniquity; for this reason God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of exultation above those who share with You. And: You, O Lord, in the beginning founded the earth, and the works of Your hands are the heavens. They will perish, but You will remain; and they will all grow old like a garment, and like a mantle You will change them, and they will be changed; but You are the very same, and Your years will not fail.

a.g: having become so much better than the Angels
a name more excellent than they
let all the Angels of God adore Him
God, Your God, has anointed You
